title: Finite normal integral generator trees for alteration covers
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Suppose its affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$. Let $(T_b\to X)_{b\in B}$ be a covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/X$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. There is a finite rooted tree, whose vertices are labelled by nonempty integral Noetherian schemes of finite type over $X$ and whose edges are $X$-morphisms from a child to its parent. Its root is $X$. Every vertex other than the root is normal (all its local rings are integrally closed domains). Each internal vertex $Z$ has one of the following two types of children. (P) There is a single child $W$, and $W\to Z$ is proper surjective with finite function field extension of degree prime to $\ell$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. (E) The vertex $Z$ is normal and its children form a finite completely decomposed family of separated etale morphisms of finite type $Z_a\to Z$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; here completely decomposed means that every $z\in Z$ lifts to some $z_a\in Z_a$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(z_a)$. For each leaf $L$ there are $b\in B$ and an $X$-morphism $L\to T_b$. Function field means the residue field at the unique generic point [def-weil-residue-field]. A tree with just its root is permitted when such a leaf map exists.

source.place: Expose II, §§1.2.5--1.2.8 and 2.3.1, Corollary 2.2.4, Proposition 3.1.1 and §3.1.2, printed pp. 25--29: finite iterated generating covers with normal integral vertices; §3.1.2 permits completely decomposed etale generators. No proper-then-etale global normal form is asserted.
